summary: The remaining screen is owned by the unported whole function potion.c:make_sick, called by the SICK arm of wizcmds.c:wiz_intrinsic after the menu selection is confirmed. With no prior Sick timeout, wiz_intrinsic supplies 30; the recorded rn2(2)=1 selects SICK_NONVOMITABLE. make_sick sets the timed Sick intrinsic and type, prints “You feel deathly sick.”, calls exercise(A_CON, FALSE) for the missing rn2(2) draw, and stores #wizintrinsic with KILLED_BY delayed attribution. At expiry, timeout.c:nh_timeout decrements the property, skips recovery for nonvomitable sickness, transfers the saved delayed killer to game-over state, and ends with done_timeout(POISONING, SICK).

source.branch: The wizard-mode #wizintrinsic SICK arm is reached after a confirmed menu pick; Sick_resistance is false, the prior Sick timeout is zero, and the positive timeout is 30. The call passes the selected sickness type and cause string #wizintrinsic.
dependencies: potion.c:set_itimeout: void state update; writes the timeout field of u.uprops[SICK].intrinsic through itimeout().
attrib.c:exercise: void state/RNG side effect; exercise(A_CON, FALSE) is called while Sick remains and consumes rn2(2) at attrib.c:509 when |AEXE(A_CON)| < AVAL.
end.c:find_delayed_killer: returned struct kinfo pointer is consumed as kptr to decide whether to replace the pending SICK cause and whether to deallocate it on cure.
end.c:delayed_killer: void state update; stores the SICK delayed-killer cause and its prefix.
end.c:dealloc_killer: void state update; removes the saved SICK cause when the property clears.
strcmp: return is consumed to use KILLED_BY for cause #wizintrinsic and KILLED_BY_AN for other causes.

evidence: The supplied C recording challenges/cases/v15/wizard-sets-sick-intrinsic-confirmed.session.json, segment 0 steps 15–17, shows the “Which intrinsics?” menu, the e selection marker on “fatally sick”, then Enter confirming it; step 17 emits “You feel deathly sick.” and records rn2(2)=1 at wizcmds.c:1036 followed by rn2(2)=1 at exercise(attrib.c:509). The supplied diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v15/wizard-sets-sick-intrinsic-confirmed.json reports that exact step-17 first mismatch, 17/18 screens matched, and unported potion.c make_sick.

At wizcmds.c:973–997, properties are listed and PICK_ANY is presented; lines 1000–1017 convert the confirmed pick to a property and derive/clamp its timeout. With this property initially unset and the default count, newtimeout is 30. Lines 1035–1037 choose SICK_NONVOMITABLE for the recorded rn2(2)=1 and call make_sick(newtimeout, "#wizintrinsic", TRUE, typ).

The complete source owner is potion.c:137–191. For positive timeout and no Sick_resistance, make_sick emits the newly-sick message when Sick was zero, stores the timed intrinsic with set_itimeout, ORs the sickness kind into u.usick_type, and marks disp.botl. It then finds the SICK delayed-killer record and, while Sick remains, calls exercise(A_CON, FALSE).

attrib.c:488–518 defines exercise; line 509 applies -rn2(2) for a decrement when the attribute exercise value is below AVAL. This is the second recorded draw missing after the JS wizcmds.js:402–407 branch currently draws the type and only calls note_unported("potion.c make_sick").

The timer and cause are consumed later by timeout.c:671–723: nh_timeout decrements every timed intrinsic, handles SICK expiry, permits recovery only when SICK_NONVOMITABLE is absent, transfers the delayed killer into svk.killer, calls done_timeout(POISONING, SICK), and clears u.usick_type. In potion.c:184–188, #wizintrinsic selects KILLED_BY and is stored with delayed_killer; end.c:1707–1734 defines that record and its lookup, while timeout.c:571–585 sends the final cause through done().
